title: Are You Using Reliable Graph Prompts? Trojan Prompt Attacks on Graph Neural Networks

problem.claim: Graph Prompt Learning models may be vulnerable to backdoor attacks that manipulate model behavior through hidden triggers.

gap.claim: Existing graph backdoor attacks modify model parameters during training, which is impractical when GNN encoder parameters are frozen in Graph Prompt Learning, and downstream users may further fine-tune task models on clean datasets.

contributions.claim: TGPA is a backdoor attack framework designed specifically for Graph Prompt Learning.
TGPA injects backdoors into graph prompts without modifying pre-trained GNN encoders.
TGPA includes a fine-tuning-resistant poisoning approach intended to preserve backdoor effectiveness after downstream model adjustments.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that TGPA ensures high attack success rates and clean accuracy.
The authors report that TGPA remains effective after downstream model fine-tuning.
The authors report extensive experiments on multiple datasets and under various settings demonstrating TGPA's effectiveness against Graph Prompt Learning models with fixed GNN encoders.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph Prompt Learning adapts pre-trained GNN models to downstream tasks using prompts without full-model fine-tuning.
The vulnerability of Graph Prompt Learning to backdoor attacks has received limited attention.
Parameter-modification attacks are impractical with frozen encoders, and downstream fine-tuning on clean data complicates attacks.
The paper proposes TGPA, which poisons graph prompts and adds resistance to downstream fine-tuning without modifying pre-trained encoders.
Experiments across multiple datasets and settings are reported to demonstrate TGPA's effectiveness.

source_observation.claim: When core model parameters are frozen, the attack surface may shift to task-specific prompts.

interpretation.claim: Adaptation mechanisms can introduce distinct security risks even when the underlying pre-trained encoder is unchanged.

application.claim: Security evaluation of parameter-efficient adaptation should examine prompts and other downstream adaptation artifacts, not only base-model parameters.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these risks generalize beyond the reported Graph Prompt Learning settings.

source_observation.claim: Downstream fine-tuning on clean data can complicate the persistence of a backdoor.

interpretation.claim: Robustness to legitimate downstream adaptation is a relevant dimension for evaluating backdoor attacks.

application.claim: Attack evaluations should include downstream adjustment conditions when users can fine-tune task models.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the fine-tuning procedures, parameter ranges, or conditions under which resistance holds.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, attack success rates, clean accuracy values, or experimental settings.
The abstract does not describe the poisoning procedure, trigger construction, or fine-tuning protocol.
